notes: Sample capacity_policy.json - when a projected disk or tablespace exhaustion becomes a finding. Copy to capacity_policy.json and edit.

A forecast is only worth alerting on when it is close enough to act before it arrives, and 'close enough' is a property of your organisation, not of the disk: critical is 'inside the time it takes to buy, provision or free space', warning is 'plan it into the next maintenance window'. That is why these are two numbers in a config file and not a constant in the collector.
'reserve_gb' is space subtracted before the projection, for a volume that must never actually reach zero.

'overrides' match on server_id plus 'item' (a drive letter, a mount point, or a tablespace name). Per-volume overrides exist because a 4 TB data volume and a 60 GB system volume are not the same problem: the same 'days to full' means a shrug on one and a weekend on the other.

overrides._note: A log volume that fell from 618 GB to 163 GB in three days during a backup-chain break needs the shortest notice you can give it, and 50 GB held back so the instance keeps running while somebody reacts.
A large, slow-growing archive volume. Ninety days of warning is noise here; the interesting signal is the month before it fills.
